source_text: Quem igitur parvulorum confiteris auctorem? Deum verum? Sed malum ille non fecit Sed naturam hominis ipse non condidit Si mala commixtio, deformis et conditio corporum et ideo corpora quoque malo a te deputantur auctori Deus vero divisit in sexu, quod in operatione coniungeret. Ab ipso igitur commixtio corporum, a quo est origo corporum Tot ergo rerum bonarum, id est, corporum, sexuum, coniunctionum malos fructus esse non posse nec homines ob hoc a Deo fieri,ut a diabolo, sicut dicis legitimo iure teneantur". Iam dictum est non eos ideo teneri, quia homines sunt, quod naturae nomen est, cuius
pass_a_gloss: Whom therefore do you confess as author of the little ones? The true God? But he did not make evil. [Or the devil?] But he himself did not found the nature of the human being. If mixing is evil, the condition of bodies is also deformed, and therefore bodies too are assigned by you to an evil author. God in fact divided in sex what he would join in working. Therefore the mixing of bodies is from him from whom is the origin of bodies. So many good things, that is bodies, sexes, joinings, cannot have evil fruits, nor are human beings made by God for this, that they be held by the devil by lawful right, as you say.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis
LS parvulus; Blaise infants in original-sin debate

pass_b_english: Whom, then, do you confess to be the creator of infants? The true God? But he did not make evil.
[Or the devil?] But he did not create human nature.
If union is evil, the condition of bodies is shameful too; so you also assign bodies to an evil creator.
God distinguished by sex what he would unite in action. Therefore bodily union comes from the one from whom bodies originate.
So many good things—bodies, sexes, unions—cannot have evil fruits. Nor are human beings made by God so that the devil may possess them under a lawful claim, as you say.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

choices.why: Speechless newborns without rational choice; Julian's test case against inherited sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.
